editorial:
Imagine you are at the top of your game, playing the biggest basketball matches of your high school life, and then everything just crashes down. That is exactly what happens to Tom Irvin. You get to see him go from a star athlete to someone who is completely lost after a traumatic encounter with sexual misconduct. The movie feels very heavy and personal, putting you right in the middle of Tom's head as he tries to figure out who he even is anymore. It is not a typical sports movie; it is more about the mental battle of surviving something terrible and trying to find a way back to normal.

What really works here is the acting, as you can feel the pain and confusion on screen. The pacing is a bit slow at times, but it helps you feel how stuck Tom feels in his own life. If you like stories that deal with real-life struggles and emotional growth, you should definitely check this out. You can rent it on Apple TV for a quick watch, or if you want the best picture quality, try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to see every detail.
endingExplained: By the end, you see Tom finally stop running from his pain. He faces the truth about what happened to him and starts the long process of healing. The final scenes show him letting go of the version of himself that the world expected him to be. He does not magically fix everything, but he finds a sense of peace and regains his identity, showing that recovery is a slow journey.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves serious character studies and stories about overcoming trauma.
